A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ubiquitin‐dependent and ubiquitin‐independent mechanisms of receptor internalization can be distinguished by the fate of the receptor following internalization: the former mechanism delivers the receptor to the vacuo/lysosome, while the latter leads to receptor recycling.
ubiquitination serves as an internal signal to direct the receptor into the constitutive endocytic pathway, while it is not required for the ligand‐mediated endocytic uptake.
ubiquitination of the receptor triggers its delivery to the vacuoles by a pathway which is independent of ligand‐binding and which is distinct from the ligand‐independence pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ubiquitination of the a‐factor receptor is not a requirement for its internalization into the recycling pathway, and that the ubiquitinated receptor is not required for recycling itself.
the ligand‐inhibited recycling pathway is a ubiquitin‐independent pathway.
ubiquitin is a versatile and flexible post‐translational modification, with multiple, context‐dependent roles.
